title: Information Security Overview
subject: Cybersecurity
summary: Information security combines art and science to protect information assets through policies, education, and technology. It involves multiple stakeholders and addresses both technical and human factors in organizational systems.

nodes.label: Information Security
nodes.desc: Protection of information assets using policy, education, and technology to maintain confidentiality, integrity, and availability

nodes.label: CIA Triad
nodes.desc: Core security principles: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability that must be protected at all times

nodes.label: Information Systems
nodes.desc: Composed of hardware, software, data, people, procedures, and networks that process information

nodes.label: Top-Down Security
nodes.desc: Security implementation driven by upper management as opposed to grassroots efforts

nodes.label: Communities of Interest
nodes.desc: Groups united by similar interests within organizations, including management and IT professionals

nodes.label: Security as Art
nodes.desc: Security implementation without hard rules or universal solutions, relying on individual perception and experience

nodes.label: Security as Science
nodes.desc: Security based on specific conditions and interactions of hardware/software that can be systematically resolved

nodes.label: Social Science in Security
nodes.desc: Examines human behavior and interactions with systems as critical factors in security effectiveness

nodes.label: Data Owners
nodes.desc: Responsible for security and use of specific information sets within the organization

nodes.label: Data Custodians
nodes.desc: Responsible for storage, maintenance, and protection of information assets

nodes.label: Data Trustees
nodes.desc: Appointed to oversee information management and coordinate with custodians for storage and protection

nodes.label: Data Users
nodes.desc: Work with information to perform daily jobs and support organizational mission
